hook: These Marines were a few steps from a burning forest.
narration: These Marines were working a few steps from a burning forest.
It was the Creek Fire, in the Sierra National Forest in California, in September 2020.
About two hundred fifty Marines and sailors from Camp Pendleton were sent to help fight it.
Ground crews like this scrape a line down to bare dirt, so when the flames get there, nothing is left to burn.
Where the fire crept across, they hit it with hoses.
[short pause] The Creek Fire grew to more than three hundred fifty thousand acres.
outcome: After a month on the fire lines, the Marines and sailors returned to Camp Pendleton.
title: Marines inside a burning forest
description:
On Sept. 24, 2020, Marines and sailors from the 7th Engineer Support Battalion worked the Creek Fire in California's Sierra National Forest alongside National Interagency Fire Center crews. About 250 of them helped fight the fire before returning to Camp Pendleton after a month-long mission.

Footage: U.S. Marine Corps video by Lance Cpl. Kevin N. Seidensticker, 1st Marine Logistics Group, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/767280/7th-engineer-support-battalion-conducts-wildland-fire-fighting-operations-with-national-interagency-fire-center-personnel-day-six
